summary: Tsukasa Mizushima, an indologist and historian, studied at the University of Tokyo (graduating around 1976 and completing his doctorate by 1992). He taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Allione works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Antioch University (around 1980–1982) and under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu. She founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a position as senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and is attested as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang in 1987.

Tsultrim Kelsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University (attested 1984–2002, serving as professor), and Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (around 1962–1971). He held positions at Doshisha University (around 1978–1993) and served as professor at Kyoto University (around 1993–2007).

Tsuruji Sahoda, a specialist in Indology and philosophy, studied at Kyoto University from around 1922 to 1925. He later held academic posts at Ritsumeikan University (around 1928–1949) and Osaka University (around 1949–1963).
Tsutomu Hatai worked in Indology and other fields. Attested in 1987, he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society.
Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University, where he is attested in 1990.

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber (around 1908–1914) and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, and Toyo University.

Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Hokkaido University. He held positions as a collaborative researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and held an appointment as a special appointment researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).
Tsyben Zhamtsarano was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902. He later headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming works in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai and Harvard universities, later teaching at Princeton, UC Berkeley, and Harvard (1981–2010), while directing the Harvard-Yenching Institute and holding a chair professorship at Peking University.

Tubten Chokyi Dorje was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught numerous disciples, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Tubten Nyendrak was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and his students included Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima studied under traditional teachers Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.

Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912 and was affiliated with Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under teachers Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
